rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revival returned the man's soul to his body as a special life; prophets' bodies do not decay, and this extraordinary event differs from resurrection at the Gathering.
rows.anchor: أي أحياه وهي حياة خاصة ردت بها روحه إلى جسده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He believed he had stayed a day or part of one either through knowledge God imparted or because he remembered sleeping in the morning and waking near evening.
rows.anchor: اعتقد ذلك بعلم أودعه الله فيه أو لأنه تذكر أنه نام في أول النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to inspect the unchanged food and drink prompts reflection; they may have accompanied him, been placed in an honored grave, or been with him when God caused him to die.
rows.anchor: أي فانظره في حال أنه لم يتسنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لم يتسنه means unchanged; it derives from year because years bring change, its final h is radical, and the form أسنت means afflicted by famine, illustrated by a line attributed to Matrūd al-Khuzāʿī or Ibn al-Zibaʿrā.
rows.anchor: أصله مشتق من السنة لأن مر السنين يوجب التغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says the donkey had decayed until only bones remained, then God revived it before the man's eyes; simply seeing it sufficed as evidence.
rows.anchor: كان حماره قد بلي فلم تبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God displayed three forms of revival: restoring the man's body by returning its soul, preserving the food, and restoring the donkey; this was a sign for the convinced, and perhaps some elect witnessed it.
rows.anchor: وقد جمع الله له أنواع الإحياء إذ أحيى جسده بنفخ الروح عن غير إعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولنجعلك آية is coordinated with an implied command to inspect the donkey: the food, drink, and donkey were a sign to him, while his verified person became a sign to others.
rows.anchor: معطوف على مقدر دل عليه قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bones may be those of dead humans; alternatively, the definite article can stand for a possessive, making them the donkey's bones and the phrase an appositive to donkey.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن المراد عظام بعض الآدميين الذين هلكوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most of the ten readers read ننشرها with rāʾ, meaning revive; Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, ʿĀṣim, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read ننشزها with zāy, meaning raise, so the readings supply two related senses.
rows.anchor: بالراء مضارع أنشر الرباعي بمعنى الإحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book of Ezekiel similarly describes bones joining, then being covered with sinew and flesh and finally skin.
rows.anchor: فتقاربت العظام كل عظم إلى عظمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read أعلم with hamzat al-qaṭʿ as the man's present-tense statement, renewing knowledge he had previously attained after seeing the sign.
rows.anchor: قرأ الجمهور أعلم بهمزة قطع على أنه مضارع علم فيكون جواب الذي مر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read أعلم with hamzat al-waṣl as God's speech; although coordination with the command to look was expected, it is omitted because this statement is the conclusion of the evidence.
rows.anchor: وقرأه حمزة والكسائي بهمزة وصل على أنه من كلام الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham is another example of God as believers' protector and a second example following the village episode; the implied comparison is to Abraham asking to see resurrection.
rows.anchor: فإن إبراهيم لفرط محبته الوصول إلى مرتبة المعاينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Out of intense desire for direct certainty, Abraham sought to move from theoretical demonstrative knowledge to necessary, sensory knowledge of the dead being revived.
rows.anchor: فسأل الله أن يريه إحياء الموتى بالمحسوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here كيف is an adverbial of state without interrogative force, as in God's shaping of people in the womb however He wills.
rows.anchor: على الحال مجردة عن الاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reward and blessing of spending are compared to a seed yielding seven ears of a hundred grains each; fertile soil and rain are omitted because they are implicit, making an intelligible reward visible through a familiar scene.
rows.anchor: وقد شبه حال إعطاء النفقة ومصادفتها موقعها وما أعطي من الثواب لهم بحال حبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seed is the basis of the image because its increase comes from within; beneficence is commonly likened to planting, as the proverb says that a planter may not harvest.
rows.anchor: وجعل أصل التمثيل في التضعيف حبة لأن تضعيفها من ذاتها لا بشيء يزاد عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The single baseline for multiplication is the reward for even the least good deed, such as intending a good deed without doing it; spending in God's path earns seven hundredfold.
rows.anchor: الوحدة هنا هي ما يثيب الله به على الحسنات الصغيرة

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī and others report that the verse concerned ʿUthmān and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, who equipped the army of hardship before Tabūk with substantial donations.
rows.anchor: الواحدي في أسباب النزول وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's multiplication has many degrees known only to Him, varying with donor, recipient, time, place, sincerity, obedience, goodwill, and self-sacrifice.
rows.anchor: المضاعفة درجات كثيرة لا يعلمها إلا الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the description of those who spend emphasizes the importance of this quality.
rows.anchor: أعاد قوله : { الذين ينفقون أموالهم في سبيل الله } إظهارا للاهتمام بهذه الصلة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains ثم as rank-order rather than elapsed time: leaving off reminders and harm is more exalted than the act of giving, which can gratify the donor's vanity.
rows.anchor: لإظهار التفاوت بين الإنفاق وترك المن والأذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mann originally meant favor or generosity, then came to mean recalling one's benefaction to its recipient; after charity it has that latter sense.
rows.anchor: ثم أطلق على عد الإنعام على المنعم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mann in spending includes boasting to Muslims or those equipped for battle, but not praising a fighter's service or his people's contribution; poems by al-Ḥuraysh and ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās illustrate the distinction.
rows.anchor: وإنما يكون المن في الإنفاق في سبيل الله بالتطاول على المسلمين والرياء بالإنفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harm means injuring recipients in word or deed; the discussion begins a poetic illustration by al-Nābigha.
rows.anchor: والأذى هو أن يؤذي المنفق من أنفق عليه بإساءة في القول أو في الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion moves from spending in God's path to charity for needy individuals, where reminders and injury are more likely because donor and recipient know one another personally.
rows.anchor: تخلص من غرض التنويه بالإنفاق في سبيل الله إلى التنويه بضرب آخر من الإنفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mann toward a recipient is reminding them of the favor, as already explained.
rows.anchor: فالمن على المتصدق عليه هو تذكيره بالنعمة كما تقدم آنفا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī's wordplay contrasts the sweetness of blessings with the bitterness of reminding: الآلاء first means blessings, then a bitter plant; المن first means manna from heaven and then reminding of a favor.
rows.anchor: طعم الآلاء أحلى من المن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adhā is injury or slight harm; here it means explicit condescension, reproaching poverty, or humiliating the recipient, distinct from the reminder itself.
rows.anchor: والأذى الإساءة والضر القليل للمنعم عليه

rows.speaker: أبو حامد الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazālī locates the root of reminders in the heart and their outward forms in speech and action; resentment at giving and feeling superior to the poor both arise from ignorance of charity's greater reward and of true human worth.
rows.anchor: إلى أن المن له أصل ومغرس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence is an explanatory resumption; the indefinite قول معروف minimizes the standard, so even a little kind speech is better than charity followed by harm.
rows.anchor: إلى آخرها مستأنفة استئنافا بيانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Known good speech is what people recognize as acceptable, namely gracious speech, the opposite of injury.
rows.anchor: فالمراد به القول الحسن وهو ضد الأذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiveness may mean the donor overlooking an insistent or rude beggar, or God overlooking sins because charity was accompanied by kind speech; injury may thus erase charity's reward.
rows.anchor: والمغفرة هنا يراد بها التجاوز عن الإساءة أي تجاوز المتصدق عن الملح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's richness and forbearance urge believers to rise above stinginess and to pardon the roughness of some recipients.
rows.anchor: تذييل للتذكير بصفتين من صفات الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Invalidity means failure of a deed's intended legal effect: an obligatory act is not discharged if a pillar or condition fails, while a voluntary act loses reward when a legal impediment prevents it, as here.
rows.anchor: فمعنى بطلان العمل عدم ترتب أثره الشرعي عليه سواء كان العمل واجبا أم كان متطوعا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison phrase is a settled circumstantial expression describing the addressees: do not act like one who spends for people's eyes and disbelieves in God and the Last Day.
rows.anchor: في إتباع صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative expression denotes a whole class, not a particular person; the comparison vilifies the example and does not make the legal ruling identical, preserving other evidence.
rows.anchor: مراد به جنس وليس مراد به معينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Riyāʾ is an intensive form from seeing, describing frequent display of good deeds; the hamza may be replaced by yāʾ after kasra, producing رياء.
rows.anchor: وهو أن يكثر من إظهار أعماله الحسنة للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims who seek reward but follow charity with reminders and harm are compared with unbelievers who give only for show and praise, seeking no afterlife reward.
rows.anchor: والمعنى تشبيه بعض المتصدقين المسلمين الذين يتصدقون طلبا للثواب ويعقبون صدقاتهم بالمن والأذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither group benefits beyond gratifying pride over the weak or the habit of harming them; the image of the rock and washed-away soil extends from unbelieving show-offs to harmful donors.
rows.anchor: ووجه الشبه عدم الانتفاع مما أعطوا بأزيد من شفاء ما في صدورهم من حب التطاول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rock's thin soil looks fit for planting, but a downpour washes it away and leaves smooth bare stone, frustrating the farmer's hope; the image's pronoun can refer to the spender because the parable also depicts the analogue.
rows.anchor: فحذفت صفة التراب إيجازا اعتمادا على أن التراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The more precise image is a rock concealed beneath apparently fertile soil, which the rain strips away; this differs from simply picturing soil on rock being swept off, as in a separate context at 14:18.
rows.anchor: وهذا أحسن وأدق من أن نجعل المعنى تمثيل إنفاق الكافر بحال تراب على صفوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the comparison particle can describe an implied noun for spending, with a possessive omitted before the relative phrase: spending like the one who spends for show.
rows.anchor: صفة لمصدر محذوف دل عليه ما في لفظ صدقاتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This image reverses the earlier seed yielding seven hundred grains, pairing the two pictures of failed and fruitful spending.
rows.anchor: وقد روعي في هذا التمثيل عكس التمثيل لمن ينفق ماله في سبيل الله بحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The compound comparison maps a promising hope that yields nothing onto the donor's hope for reward, which heedlessness can ruin by prompting reminders and harm.
rows.anchor: ووجه الشبه الأمل في حالة تغر بالنفع ثم لا تلبث ألا تأتي لآملها بما أمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لا يقدرون على شيء مما كسبوا is deliberately flexible: it may be a state of the spenders, of the figurative rock, an explanatory resumption, a summary, or a state with an omitted relative pronoun.
rows.anchor: وصالحا لأن يجعل استينافا بيانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cannot retrieve what they gave or benefit from its reward, so nothing remains for them.
rows.anchor: لا يستطيعون أن يسترجعوه ولا انتفعوا بثوابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible sense is that they fail to place their earnings where they belong, spending fruitlessly for the afterlife, as the next statement about disbelievers' guidance suggests.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى لا يحسنون وضع شيء مما كسبوا موضعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bare rock yields no crop, as in the description of a person turning his hands over what he spent; God's denial of guidance to disbelievers warns believers against adopting their reminders and harm.
rows.anchor: مسوق لتحذير المؤمنين من تسرب أحوال الكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sincere spender's garden is set against the show-off spender's image to make the distance between the ranks vivid and renew praise; a more intricate picture beautifies its subject.
rows.anchor: لزيادة بيان ما بين المرتبتين من البون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier seed image is simple for swiftly picturing multiplied reward; this garden image is more involved because several favorable features enhance the scene and its analogue.
rows.anchor: ومثله فيما سلف تمثيلا غير كثير التركيب لتحصل السرعة بتخيل مضاعفة الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ابتغاء مرضاة الله and تثبيتا are circumstantial accusatives, meaning seeking God's pleasure and strengthening themselves; تثبيت depicts restraining inner hesitation and stinginess.
rows.anchor: على الحال بتأويل المصدر بالوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated practice of difficult virtues makes them firm habits; spending especially strengthens obedience because wealth is precious, and من marks a figurative partiality among states of the self.
rows.anchor: فإن إراضة النفس على فعل ما يشق عليها لها أثر في رسوخ الأعمال حتى تعتاد الفضائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual ضعفين indicates repetition rather than exactly two, like لبيك: the garden yields multiplied produce in varying measure.
rows.anchor: التثنية فيه لمجرد التكرير مثل لبيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even without heavy rain, light rain yields a lesser crop; sincere spending brings great reward that varies with sincerity and self-strengthening but never disappoints its giver.
rows.anchor: أي فإن لم يصبها مطر غزير كفاها مطر قليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The new parable answers the hearer's expectation after two favorable spending images, depicting the disgraceful opposite of sincere charity unaccompanied by reminders or harm.
rows.anchor: استئناف بياني أثاره ضرب المثل العجيب للمنفق في سبيل الله بمثل حبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its likeness is failure and despair just as hope nears its harvest, contrasting the sincere spender and illustrating the ruin of showy or injurious giving.
rows.anchor: ووجه الشبه هو حصول خيبة ويأس في وقت تمام الرجاء وإشراف الإنتاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The owner is old, unable to earn elsewhere, and has weak dependents; ضعيف means young or limited, and can also mean poor, as 2:282 and Abū Khālid al-ʿAttābī's verse show.
rows.anchor: بأنه ذو عيال فهو في حاجة إلى نفعهم وأنهم ضعفاء أي صغار إذ الضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem of al-Aʿshā heightens the old man's dependence on his garden and anticipation of its yield, sharpening the audience's sense of impending loss.
rows.anchor: وقد أصابه الكبر فلا قدرة له على الكسب غير تلك الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destructive ʿiṣār is a violent hot wind, likened emphatically to fire or the simūm; it burns the garden's trees to dry wood and brings disaster at the moment of hope.
rows.anchor: فأحرقت الجنة أي أشجارها أي صارت أعوادها يابسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أيود is a warning and repudiating question, like the question about eating a brother's flesh; the unstated analogue is someone whose charity is followed by reminders and harm.
rows.anchor: استفهام إنكار وتحذير كما في قوله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In the report of ʿUmar's question to the Companions, Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the garden as a wealthy person's good deeds, later consumed when Satan tempts him to sin near life's end; al-Bukhārī transmits the exchange.
rows.anchor: روى البخاري أن عمر بن الخطاب سأل يوما أصحاب رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Likewise signals that God clarifies signs through this kind of explanation, bringing abstract truths near through tangible images so people reflect on consequences and avoid heedlessness.
rows.anchor: نحو ما في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to spend is delayed until after admonition, encouragement, and warning; this rhetorical ordering prepares acceptance because charity was already a familiar religious duty deserving careful praise and correction.
rows.anchor: إفضاء إلى المقصود وهو الأمر بالصدقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sermon attributed to ʿAlī exhorts people to fight after Sufyān al-Ghāmidī's raid on al-Anbār and killing its governor; Ibn ʿĀshūr suspects jihad was altered from qitāl by an interpolator or mistake, since the context says fighting and he doubts ʿAlī said the transmitted word.
rows.anchor: فلعل أصلها القتال كما يدل عليه قوله بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command may require obligatory zakāt, recommend voluntary charity, or encompass both as a shared request; other evidence determines each ruling, and the qualifier good property fits all spending.
rows.anchor: والأمر يجوز أن يكون للوجوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good things means the best of each asset class, and also lawfully earned wealth; prophetic reports say God accepts only what is pure. The land-produced category needs no repeated qualifier because cultivation implies lawful effort.
rows.anchor: ويطلق الطيب على المال المكتسب بوجه حلال

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says the Merciful receives charity from pure earnings, and another report states that God is pure and accepts only what is pure.
rows.anchor: إن الله طيب لا يقبل إلا طيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Produce from the earth means crops and fruit, whether naturally grown or produced through ordinary causes such as irrigation and planting.
rows.anchor: والمراد بما أخرج من الأرض الزروع والثمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some include minerals: Mālik requires zakāt at the threshold at one-fortieth, while Abū Ḥanīfa treats minerals as non-zakāt wealth subject to one-fifth; some include buried treasure, taxed at one-fifth as booty under Mālikī law. Ibn ʿĀshūr suggests the verse likely means monetary and livestock zakāt alongside crops and fruit.
rows.anchor: وتجب على المعدن الزكاة عند مالك إذا بلغ مقدار النصاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تيمموا derives from تتيمموا with one imperfect prefix t dropped and means intend or deliberately seek.
rows.anchor: حذفت تاء المضارعة في المضارع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khabīth means the worst in a class, used of unlawful or impure things and the opposite extreme of good; its use in a prohibition covers every kind it denotes.
rows.anchor: والخبيث الشديد سوءا في صنفه فلذلك يطلق على الحرام وعلى المستقذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fronted منه in the circumstantial phrase implies exclusive targeting: do not give only inferior property; mixed property is permitted, especially for zakāt distributed across the same asset class, while livestock is assessed at average quality.
rows.anchor: قدما عليه للدلالة على الاختصاص

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In a report from the Muwaṭṭaʾ, the Prophet tells a collector who brought premium dates to sell inferior dates for dirhams and then buy premium ones, showing that zakāt is collected from each class of its own kind.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أرسل عاملا على صدقات خيبر فأتاه بتمر جنيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce تيمموا with one light t in connected and initial reading; al-Bazzī from Ibn Kathīr doubles it in connected reading.
rows.anchor: بتاء واحدة خفيفة وصلا وابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may be a statement used as an argument against giving unlawful property: just as people dislike acquiring it, they should dislike giving it; alternatively, it is a prohibition against accepting known unlawful property, which does not become lawful by transfer. Both readings imply that known unlawful wealth may not be taken.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الكلام على ظاهره من الإخبار فتكون جملة الحال تعليلا لنهيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إغماض literally means closing an eyelid and figuratively can mean ease or rest; al-Aʿshā's phrase فاغتمضي means be content or at ease.
rows.anchor: فيطلق تارة على الهناء والاستراحة لأن من لوازم الإغماض راحة النائم قال الأعشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because closing the eyes prevents seeing, إغماض can mean tolerating an objectionable thing; al-Ṭirimmāḥ uses it for people accepting humiliation.
rows.anchor: ويطلق تارة على لازمه من عدم الرؤية فيدل على التسامح في الأمر المكروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase أغمض عينه على قذى describes deliberately overlooking a severe annoyance; a poem by ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Zurāra al-Kilābī illustrates enduring it.
rows.anchor: فإذا أرادوا المبالغة في التغافل عن المكروه الشديد قالوا أغمض عينه على قذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the declarative reading, the exception restricts the negation; on the prohibitive reading, it intensifies the prohibition by seeming to allow acceptance only if one disregards the rule.
rows.anchor: وأما على الوجه الثاني من جعل النفي بمعنى النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conclusion reminds people that God needs no donations that fail to help the poor or tolerate the unlawful, yet praises those who give pure charity; أَعْلَموا draws attention or addresses those acting as if unaware.
rows.anchor: غني عن صدقاتكم التي لا تنفع الفقراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's absolute richness means one should offer Him the best, just as one would give the best to someone who needs nothing.
rows.anchor: ولله الغنى المطلق فلا يعطى لأجله ولامتثال أمره إلا خير ما يعطيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamīd may be an intensive active adjective because God greatly praises good-doers, or passive meaning praised; believers should be free of stinginess and thanked for pure charity.
rows.anchor: لأنه يثني على فاعلي الخيرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse follows the command to give good property: Satan discourages giving the best and tempts people to hoard, donate inferior goods, or fear poverty.
rows.anchor: يصد الناس عن إعطاء خيار أموالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting Satan first signals condemnation and warning, while subject-first order also strengthens the assertion that he promises poverty.
rows.anchor: وقدم اسم الشيطان مسندا إليه لأن تقديمه مؤذن بذم الحكم الذي سيق له الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's promise is a figurative assurance that poverty will follow spending, modeled on God's genuine promise; it reflects the certainty conveyed by a promise.
rows.anchor: فشبه إلقاء الشيطان في نفوسهم توقع الفقر بوعد منه بحصوله لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If promise can refer to good and evil, as al-Qāmūs follows Thaʿlab's Faṣīḥ, the expression has one figure; if promise is only good, as al-Zamakhsharī says in al-Asās, it has two.
rows.anchor: كان الوعد يطلق على التعهد بالخير والشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poverty derives from breaking the backbone, portraying incapacity; the word has several vocalizations, and فقير can function as a verbal-noun adjective.
rows.anchor: شدة الحاجة إلى لوازم الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faḥshāʾ names a very vile act or utterance deserving blame; it comes from exceeding limits and does not mean miserliness, though a miser can be called fāḥish. Satan's command is figurative whispering, not literal speech, and the definite article marks the class.
rows.anchor: اسم لفعل أو قول شديد السوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's real promise of forgiveness and bounty contrasts with Satan's temptation; placing God's name first likewise strengthens the assertion.
rows.anchor: لإظهار الفرق بين ما تدعو إليه وساوس الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wāsiʿ means abundant in grace and giving, as in the prayer that God's mercy and knowledge encompass all things; a report describes the Prophet as expansive in warmth and character.
rows.anchor: والوصف بالواسع مشتق من وسع المتعدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wisdom verse concludes and supplements the spending teachings, highlighting their value and that God has made the audience wise through guidance after ignorance.
rows.anchor: هذه الجملة اعتراض وتذييل لما تضمنته آيات الإنفاق من المواعظ والآداب

rows.speaker: الفخر
rows.claim: Al-Fakhr says reason and wisdom favor God's promise, while appetite and sensation favor Satan's call to present pleasure; the verse after God's promise identifies forgiveness and bounty as wisdom gifted by God.
rows.anchor: وجب ترجيح وعد الرحمن على وعد الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom is perfected knowledge coupled with action that follows it; its root is judgment that restrains error, as in the divine book's perfected verses and the bit in a horse's mouth.
rows.anchor: إتقان العلم وإجراء الفعل على وفق ذلك العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives wisdom to people whose sound, balanced minds can grasp truth without desire, partisanship, obstinacy, or pride, and facilitates teachers and a safe setting while removing barriers to understanding.
rows.anchor: قابلا لفهم الحقائق منقادا إلى الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom is also defined as knowing realities as far as human capacity allows, without confusing similar truths or mistaking causes and reasons.
rows.anchor: وفسرت الحكمة بأنها معرفة حقائق الأشياء على ما هي عليه بما تبلغه الطاقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion of wind was given earlier at 2:164; here ṣirr is deadly severe cold that leaves plants looking burned, whereas ṣarṣar is a fierce wind that may be cold.
rows.anchor: البرد الشديد المميت لكل زرع أو ورق يهب عليه

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf permits ṣirr to mean cold wind synonymously with ṣarṣar; Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects the usage because al-Asās and al-Rāghib do not attest it.
rows.anchor: في الكشاف } أن يكون الصر هنا اسما للريح الباردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying the wind contains ṣirr conveys exceptionally intense cold, as if it carried cold itself to the crop.
rows.anchor: حتى كأن جنس الصر مظروف فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥarth is a verbal noun used for its object: cultivated land, meaning the crop or field that the wind struck; its meanings were discussed at 3:14.
rows.anchor: والحرث هنا مصدر بمعنى المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ظلموا أنفسهم is an inserted moral description that heightens condemnation, not part of the depicted wind-and-crop image; poets also add details that do not affect a comparison, as Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr does of water.
rows.anchor: إدماج في خلال التمثيل يكسب التمثيل تفظيعا وتشويها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because listeners know the punishment of self-wrongdoers is severe, the phrase serves as admonition; the spending image explains why unbelievers' wealth and children cannot save them.
rows.anchor: والسامعون عالمون بأن عقاب الأقوام الذين ظلموا أنفسهم غاية في الشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not wrong the unbelievers by rejecting their spending: they caused this outcome by lacking faith, a condition for accepted deeds, after being informed and warned; this confirms God's promise not to wrong anyone.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أن الله لم يظلمهم حين لم يتقبل نفقاتهم بل هم تسببوا في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls هو a separator pronoun, but al-Zajjāj, as quoted by al-Ṭībī, restricts separator pronouns to subject-predicate constructions; Abū al-Baqāʾ instead treats it as the first object, with nominative replacing accusative.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري ( هو ) ضمير فصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to stinginess inferred from يبخلون, as in the statement that justice is nearer to piety; when read as a separator, one object of حساب is omitted, with its wording depending on the recitation.
rows.anchor: عائد على البخل المستفاد من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bukhl is withholding money without compensation; withholding non-monetary things is metaphorical. The word has regional vowel variants, and the Qurʾān uses the non-Ḥijāzī pattern; a prophetic report calls one who withholds blessings upon the Prophet a miser.
rows.anchor: فهو الانقباض عن إعطاء المال بدون عوض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase بل هو شر لهم reinforces that stinginess is not good and rules out an imagined middle ground between good and evil, a familiar Arabic rhetorical pattern illustrated by Imruʾ al-Qays.
rows.anchor: تأكيد لنفي كونه خيرا ، كقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سيطوقون may mean they will bear what they withheld as a burden beyond capacity, but more likely it means their wealth will become collars around their necks as punishment; either way the shame is exposed before the gathering.
rows.anchor: والأظهر أنه مشتق من الطوق ، وهو ما يلبس تحت الرقبة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet warns that whoever wrongfully takes a handspan of land will have it placed around his neck from seven earths on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: من اغتصب شبرا من أرض طوقه من سبع أرضين يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's inheritance of heaven and earth reminds misers that wealth belongs to Him and everyone leaves it behind; His enduring ownership and knowledge make the passage warning, threat, and promise.
rows.anchor: بأن المال مال الله ، وما من بخيل إلا سيذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next passage addresses Jews who said God was poor to evade encouragement to charity; the speaker may have been Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab in response to the loan verse, or Finḥāṣ ibn ʿĀzūrāʾ to Abū Bakr, after which Abū Bakr struck him and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: والذين قالوا ذلك هم اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse turns from the surah's preceding topics to reflection on creation and its signs, honoring those who heed them; this broad shift signals the surah's ending, which appropriately closes with admonition.
rows.anchor: انتقل به من المقدمات والمقصد والمتخللات بالمناسبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن emphasizes the importance of the report; creation may mean the ordered effects of making the heavens and earth or created things themselves, as in 31:11, while ulu al-albāb are people of perfected intellect.
rows.anchor: وهو النظام الذي جعل فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs in creation and alternating night and day were discussed at 2:164; remembering God can mean verbal remembrance or inward reflection.
rows.anchor: وقد قدمنا في سورة البقرة بيان ما في خلق السماوات والأرض واختلاف الليل والنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Standing, sitting, and lying on their sides means all ordinary human states of work, rest, and sleep; the alternative that these are prayer postures for able and incapacitated people is unlikely in this context.
rows.anchor: عموم الأحوال كقولهم : ضربه الظهر والبطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion of repentance continues from the prior instruction to turn away after offenders repent, and recalls its fuller treatment at 3:90; إنما restricts the promise.
rows.anchor: جر إليه قوله : { فإن تابا وأصلحا فأعرضوا عنهما }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In التوبة على الله, على metaphorically expresses a binding commitment: God promises acceptance by grace, not an obligation imposed on Him; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says such self-imposed obligations are scriptural, not rational.
rows.anchor: المعنى : التوبة تحق على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction covers those who do wrong in ignorance and repent soon; ignorance means rash or unjust conduct that stains the sin, not lacking knowledge that the act is forbidden, since an unaware person is not sinful until taught.
rows.anchor: والجهالة تطلق على سوء المعاملة وعلى الإقدام على العمل دون روية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem of ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm uses ignorance for retaliatory wrongdoing, confirming that the word can mean injustice rather than mere lack of knowledge.
rows.anchor: ألا لا يجهلن أحد علينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min qarīb means from a time close to the sinful deed; some instead interpret it as before death, taking the following phrase about death as its explanation.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { من قريب } ، من فيه للابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some held the two qualifiers abrogated by 4:48; most treat ignorance as a descriptive feature of wrongdoing by believers. A report from Qatāda says the Companions regarded every disobedience, deliberate or not, as ignorance; Ibn ʿĀshūr says both qualifiers advise normal conduct rather than condition acceptance, and the two verses leave no middle category.
rows.anchor: والأكثر على أن قيد ( بجهالة ) كوصف كاشف لعمل السوء

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmits Qatāda's report that the Companions agreed every act of disobedience is ignorance, whether deliberate or otherwise.
rows.anchor: روى عبد الرزاق عن قتادة قال : اجتمع أصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites say sincere repentance is certainly accepted on rational grounds, reasoning that otherwise God would leave a repentant person in error and punishment; Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects this as confused because the question concerns pardon for past deserved punishment.
rows.anchor: فأما المعتزلة فقالوا : التوبة الصادقة مقبولة قطعا بدليل العقل

rows.speaker: الأشعري
rows.claim: One Sunni group, including al-Ashʿarī, al-Ghazālī, al-Rāzī, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya and his father, holds acceptance certain through the combined force of many revealed texts, though each report alone may be probabilistic.
rows.anchor: وإلى هذا ذهب الأشعري ، والغزالي والرازي ، وابن عطية ووالده أبو بكر ابن عطية

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الباقلاني
rows.claim: Another Sunni group, including al-Bāqillānī, Imām al-Ḥaramayn, al-Māzirī, al-Taftāzānī, al-Fihrī, and Ibn al-Faras, says acceptance is probabilistic because multiple apparent texts do not yield certainty; Ibn ʿĀshūr considers this the sounder view but says the issue is not a creed requiring certainty.
rows.anchor: وذهب جماعة إلى أن القبول ظني لا قطعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative in فأولئك makes the audience recall the preceding qualities of fear of God and eagerness for His pleasure, marking them as deserving acceptance; the phrasing resembles 2:5 and reaffirms 4:17.
rows.anchor: للتنبيه على استحضارهم باعتبار الأوصاف المتقدمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following statement denies acceptance for repentance made at death, when life is despaired of, because repentance should lead to righteous conduct in this world and has no benefit once life is lost.
rows.anchor: تنبيه على نفي القبول عن نوع من التوبة وهي التي تكون عند اليأس من الحياة
